title: Odd restriction Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $f:\\mathbb F_2^n\\to\\mathbb F_2$ be a Boolean function, let $S\\subseteq[n]$ have nonzero algebraic normal form coefficient, and let $A\\subseteq S$. Restrict the corresponding real-valued sign-cube function by fixing every coordinate outside $S$ to $+1$, and take its Fourier coefficient on the free-coordinate set $A$. This coefficient is an odd integer divided by $2^{|S|}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on $\\mathbb F_2^n$
The algebraic normal form coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is nonzero
